analysis: The only change in this PR is a test-only addition in provider-swift/Tests/ProviderCoreTests/Service/ProviderModelSwitchTests.swift, head lines 683-687, inside failedCommitPreservesMatchingHashAndFingerprint. After the switch task returns, it asserts that loop.autopilotBusyReasons() does not contain .modelSwitch, and that .draining is present only when the connection dropped (unconfirmed commit). No production source is modified, so there is no new attack surface, no change to trust boundaries, and no weakening of the wire, attestation or custody controls. The assertion reinforces the fail-closed behavior already tested at line 682, where refusingNewWork stays true when the commit is unconfirmed. This relates to the T-053/TB-011 availability and stale-authorization concerns, and to TB-002 lifecycle handling. The test uses temp directories and a mock coordinator, with no secrets handled. Open question for other passes: the production implementation of autopilotBusyReasons() and the switch-task release path are outside the supplied evidence, so this test's correctness against production code was not verified here. That is a test-quality question, not a security regression.
